NO_ESCAPE.Commentary: Think of this as 50% more Doom on the target.  Will rapidly kill any target with repeated plays, making this an anti-boss card.

NULL.Commentary: Extremely efficient value package providing substantial damage as well as Weak.  Very good add in the early floors, or for any deck that wants Weak plus orb generation.

NUNCHAKU.Commentary: Energy is always valuable.  The counter persists across fights, allowing you to set up energy for Turn 1 in future combats.

NUTRITIOUS_OYSTER.Commentary: A useful boost to your starting HP, though most runs will prefer a Neow bonus that helps avoid damage in combats.

NUTRITIOUS_SOUP.Commentary: Turn your Strikes into a consistent source of free damage!  Great for decks that are Energy-starved or those that can amplify their Attack damage with Vulnerable or Strength.

OBLIVION.Commentary: A huge payoff for any deck that can spam a lot of cards.  Best with lots of Souls to both draw into this as well as activate it.  Each card played will activate Shroud and Sleight of Flesh.

ODDLY_SMOOTH_STONE.Commentary: 1 Block might not sound like much, but the benefit of this Relic adds up quickly to save you several HP per combat.  Gets better the more Block cards you have.

OFFERING.Commentary: Almost always saves you more HP than it costs by letting you get more cards in play.  If you're already winning the fight, consider not playing this.

OLD_COIN.Commentary: Enough money for 2 relics!  Unfortunately, you'll have to wait until the next shop to get the benefits.

OMNISLICE.Commentary: Think of this like an AoE card except debuffs on one target can benefit the damage on all targets.  Nice if you can only make one enemy Vulnerable.

ONE_TWO_PUNCH.Commentary: Many Ironclad decks are attack-heavy which lets this card multiply a wide variety of options.  Most effective on high-cost attacks like Bludgeon or Whirlwind.

ORANGE_DOUGH.Commentary: More options on Turn 1 are always nice.  Can generate useful Power cards like Calamity.

ORBIT.Commentary: This is about 1 energy per turn if you have the base 3 energy, and gets stronger the more energy you have.  Playing multiple copies of this card allows you to spend ludicrous amounts of energy every turn.  Just add draw!

ORICHALCUM.Commentary: An incredible Relic for Act 1.  Works in tandem with any effect that gives block at end of turn, such as Plating.   Still useful in the late game for mitigating bad draws or allowing you to spend all your energy on Power cards.

ORNAMENTAL_FAN.Commentary: Great source of added block for decks that can play 3 Attacks per turn. Consider 0-cost Attacks more seriously if you have this.

ORRERY.Commentary: A good purchase early-game or if you have an egg Relic that Upgrades cards.  Consider the known cards that are available for sale before gambling on this.

OUTBREAK.Commentary: Very solid area damage in decks that apply Poison many times.  Combine with Noxious Fumes, Envenom, or Bouncing Flask.

OUTMANEUVER.Commentary: Very significant energy generation provided you can wait a turn.  Much more useful with Retain effects allowing you to hold expensive cards.

OVERCLOCK.Commentary: Immediate draw can be useful for any deck to get powers and orbs down quickly, but this card shines the most with status-synergy cards such as Adaptation or Smokestack to get extra value from the created burn.

PACTS_END.Commentary: Area damage is generally desired at the start of a fight, when the condition of this card may not yet be met.  This is a card that performs well if re-drawn repeatedly, similar to Blood For Blood.

PAELS_BLOOD.Commentary: 1 draw per turn with no downside is always great!  Best with cards that make Energy or cards that cost 0, but any deck will appreciate this.

PAELS_CLAW.Commentary: Allows your basic Defends to become scaling blocks for the late game.  The main downside is the lack of an immediate upside compared to other choices.

PAELS_EYE.Commentary: Allows you to Exhaust problematic Starter or Curse cards if you draw a lousy hand.  Can also be used to double dip on per-turn effects like Mercury Hourglass thanks to the bonus turn.

PAELS_FLESH.Commentary: Energy per turn is excellent but this one takes a bit to kick in.  Great if your deck is more defensive and easily makes it to turn 3, or if you have other ways to get bonus Energy on turn 1 or 2.

PAELS_GROWTH.Commentary: Incredible if used on cards that have a strong one-time effect (Adrenaline, Big Bang) or ones that get better with more copies of themself (Perfected Strike, Crescent Spear).  Doesn't give you any benefit until your first Rest Site, so you must be able to survive early Act II without help.

PAELS_HORN.Commentary: Adds two clunky blocks that can be used to have a strong follow-up turn.  Limited in usefulness as the benefits are delayed by a turn and because Relax Exhausts after use.  Upgrade Relax as soon as you can for best results.

PAELS_LEGION.Commentary: Consistent additional Block when you need it most.  Gets better as your Block cards get better.  Especially useful with Blocks that work across multiple turns like Glitterstream.

PAELS_TEARS.Commentary: Bonus Energy that requires you to cut a turn short to get the full advantage.  Best if you have an initial Energy boost or cheap cards to get started.  Extremely broken with Ice Cream.

PAELS_TOOTH.Commentary: The Upgrades are good, but there is a delay before you receive them and you must be able to survive without some of your cards for a short while.  Do not use this on your 5 best cards.

PAELS_WING.Commentary: Generates a lot of Relics but takes a while to get going and you must be willing to forego card rewards.  This makes it hard to survive Act II.  Gets a lot better if you have any source of additional card rewards such as Prayer Wheel.

PAGESTORM.Commentary: Extremely effective card draw for any deck that has Ethereal cards.  Even works with Daze and Ascender's Bane.  Loves an upgrade to become 0-cost.

PALE_BLUE_DOT.Commentary: Card draw per turn is very good, but the condition that you must satisfy is a little tricky to achieve.  Works best with an abundance of 0-cost cards.  A must-upgrade card.

PANACHE.Commentary: Most characters have a hard time playing 5 cards in a turn at the start of the game.  Certain builds can turn this into an extremely effective source of damage.

PANDORAS_BOX.Commentary: Getting rid of all your basic cards is a huge advantage!  You will come out ahead almost no matter what cards you get.   This is very likely to generate multiple Rare cards.

PANIC_BUTTON.Commentary: '2 turns' includes the turn you play this, so there is actually only one turn without block.  You can still gain block from powers, potions and relics while the debuff is in effect.

PANTOGRAPH.Commentary: An excellent source of healing that usually allows you to Upgrade at the Rest Site before Boss fights.  Particularly useful on Ascension 10 because of the additional Boss battle.

PAPER_KRANE.Commentary: Extremely good damage reduction that can help at any stage of the game.  Often more effective than advertised because damage numbers round down.

PAPER_PHROG.Commentary: Most Ironclad decks will have enemies Vulnerable all the time, so this is free scaling damage!

PARRY.Commentary: Not as useful as you might think - you are generally not playing Sovereign Blade multiple times per fight.  Still, the block value is high enough that this can be crucial in the right deck.

PARRYING_SHIELD.Commentary: A great source of bonus damage that is fairly easy to activate.  Remember that you can play Block cards even if the enemy isn't attacking to get some damage.

PARSE.Commentary: Necrobinder has a lot of ways to draw cards, and this one doesn't stand out much unless you benefit from Ethereal synergies.

PARTICLE_WALL.Commentary: Reusable block that is excellent with a surplus of stars.  If you can make this card free, you immediately achieve an infinite combo of playing it over and over.  One of Regent's best block options.

PATTER.Commentary: Solid block, plus a small damage bonus that scales well with multihit cards.  Use with things like Radiate, Stardust, or Celestial Might.

PEAR.Commentary: 10 HP isn't the most exciting, but this is decent value for one relic.  Not usually worth buying for Gold.

PENDULUM.Commentary: Small but consistent card draw is nice to have. End fights with the counter on 2 to draw a card on Turn 1 of the next fight.

PEN_NIB.Commentary: This will double the damage of the whole Attack including any other bonuses or modifiers.  Gets better the stronger your best Attack is.

PERFECTED_STRIKE.Commentary: Good enough damage to add in the early game that can scale up with more Strike cards.  Great with Pommel Strike and more Perfected Strike, not great with Twin Strike or Setup Strike.

PERMAFROST.Commentary: Although it's not that much Block, the timing on this Relic is very helpful.  The added Block allows you to set up your Powers more easily to get started in fights.

PETRIFIED_TOAD.Commentary: A great relic for the early game that lets you throw 15 damage per fight.  In the late game you are more likely to want to keep other good Potions so this will have less relevance.

PHANTOM_BLADES.Commentary: Retaining your shivs lets you benefit more from the bonus damage on first Shiv, but you can also use this to line up big turns with attack relics or with Finisher.

PHIAL_HOLSTER.Commentary: The starting potions smooth out potential early-game bad luck by guaranteeing that you have potions for the first Elite as well as giving you answers in the event of a bad hand of cards.

PHILOSOPHERS_STONE.Commentary: The added enemy Strength adds up very quickly, so your deck needs to be able to leverage the additional Energy defensively in order to make this worth it.

PHOTON_CUT.Commentary: Putting a card on top of the deck is a very useful effect for regent - you can use this to try to set up combos, to smooth out your Star spending, or just to get a block card lined up for next turn.

PIERCING_WAIL.Commentary: Incredibly efficient damage reduction for 1 energy in a wide variety of fights.  Retain with Well-Laid Plans for best results.

PILLAGE.Commentary: Pommel Strike's cooler brother.  Doesn't need an upgrade and can work wonders with an attack-heavy deck.  Combine with Anger or Hellraiser.

PILLAR_OF_CREATION.Commentary: It's difficult to make enough cards to justify including this power, but works well with things like Bungle of Joy and Crash Landing.

PINPOINT.Commentary: Provides excellent damage for 1 or 0 energy if drawn alongside skills.  Great in decks with 0-cost skills.

PLANISPHERE.Commentary: A solid trickle of healing if you can path to a decent number of ? rooms.

POCKETWATCH.Commentary: Up to 3 draw per turn can be game-winning on its own.  Pick up expensive cards and carefully count your cards on each turn.  Sometimes the draw is better than playing a card.

POISONED_STAB.Commentary: An underwhelming combination of poison and immediate damage.  Takeable in the early game and useful alongside other Poison sources.

POKE.Commentary: Very usable damage for the early game.  Combos well with other Osty attacks or with cards that return cards to your hand from the discard.

POMANDER.Commentary: A solid start that will improve your early combats.  Use it on your character's unique starting card.

POMMEL_STRIKE.Commentary: Ironclad loves card draw and this is one of the better ways to get it.  Really wants an upgrade to become draw 2.

POTION_BELT.Commentary: Though this offers no immediate impact, holding more potions allows you to stockpile power for the end game gauntlet.  You can also fill up on potions at a shop before fighting Elites.

POUNCE.Commentary: Acceptable damage that becomes very efficient if you can discount a 2- or 3-cost skill.  Use this to get free Snakebite, Leg Sweep, or Nightmare.

POWER_CELL.Commentary: Basically 2 draw on Turn 1, except you have a better idea of what you're going to get.  Particularly good if you have energy-generating cards like TURBO.

PRAYER_WHEEL.Commentary: Significantly improves the value of visiting combat rooms.  Seeing more cards will let you find more Upgraded cards as well as more Rare cards.

PRECARIOUS_SHEARS.Commentary: Most characters don't want to pay this much HP at the start of the run.

PRECISE_CUT.Commentary: Play this last to maximize damage.  You can use discard effects to clear space in hand as well.  Better than Slice most of the time.

PRECISE_SCISSORS.Commentary: Most characters will want to remove Strike.  Gives you a bit more consistency throughout the run, or a head start on creating a lean deck.

PREDATOR.Commentary: 2-cost damage plus next turn draw is a good value package for the early game.  Great with Bullet Time.

PREPARED.Commentary: A very pickable discard enabler that allows you to run more Sly cards.  Worth investing an upgrade into.  Works well with Speedster as a damage source.

PREP_TIME.Commentary: The Vigor can be saved across many turns to create a large bonus on one attack.  Combine with a multi-hit attack for massive damage.

PRESERVED_FOG.Commentary: Improved overall consistency at the cost of your turn 1 draw.  Very worth it if you have Bag of Preparation or another way to improve your turn 1.

PRIMAL_FORCE.Commentary: Amazing damage in the early game but doesn't really synergize with other Ironclad cards.  Just add Vulnerable!

PRISMATIC_GEM.Commentary: Energy per turn is very nice, but this will ruin your card rewards.  It's possible to assemble fun cross-class combos with this but you are more likely to be flooded with junk Common cards.

PRODUCTION.Commentary: A great source of one-time energy to create a burst turn or let you get powers down.  Combine with card draw sources.

PROLONG.Commentary: Uses the current block you have when you play it, so it doesn't matter if you lose block during the enemy turn.  The upgraded version is extremely powerful if you can play it every turn.

PROPHESIZE.Commentary: Absolutely massive draw.  Use this to get to your 0-energy Star cards, to set up combos, or combine with additional energy such as Orbit to play a ton of cards.

PROTECTOR.Commentary: A much better card than the basic version.  Note that the HP scaling now uses Max HP instead of current HP.  A must-upgrade.

PROWESS.Commentary: A very valuable source of Dexterity, particularly for classes that don't normally have access to it.  Really wants an upgrade to be effective.

PULL_AGGRO.Commentary: A solid 2-cost block with some lasting effect in the form of Summon.  Really good with Danse Macabre or Intimidating Helmet.

PULL_FROM_BELOW.Commentary: This is a multi-hit move, so it scales well with Strength or with Enchantments.  This is heavily penalized by the negative Strength on Friendship.

PUMPKIN_CANDLE.Commentary: A solid source of Energy that requires you to sacrifice some Rest Sites.  Prolong the effect by choosing more Event spaces on the map.

PUNCH_DAGGER.Commentary: This Enchantment can be very powerful on multi-hit cards or cards that you can return to your hand.  There's no benefit until you play the Attack a 2nd time, so you must be able to re-draw your cards quickly to use this.

PURITY.Commentary: Most useful when you want to thin your deck down to create an infinite combo.  Also a useful way to deal with especially harmful curses like Bad Luck.

PUTREFY.Commentary: Necro's longest-lasting source of Weak and Vulnerable, as well as the only source of both at the same time.  Amazing with Debilitate.

PYRE.Commentary: Huge energy generation for a single setup turn allows you to tackle endgame fights much more easily.  This is a must-upgrade.

QUADCAST.Commentary: An extremely powerful card even without orb investment.  20 block from a Frost orb or 32 damage from Lightning is already powerful, but this gets really crazy with Focus or with Dark orbs.

QUASAR.Commentary: An interesting outlet for Stars that interacts with colorless card and card generation effects.   Since you pick from one of three cards, this almost always makes something useful. Can generate Power cards.

RADIANT_PEARL.Commentary: 2 Energy on a turn of your choosing is great for playing key Powers or for having a powerful burst turn.  Can be Upgraded by other cards or Relics for even more energy.

RADIATE.Commentary: Really powerful AoE that can be tricky to draw alongside your star gen.  Each trigger of this card is a separate hit, making this card go crazy with Vigor or Strength applied to your character.  Your starting relic makes this card hit three times on turn 1.

RAGE.Commentary: Tons of free block for doing what Clad already does best: playing lots of attacks.

RAINBOW.Commentary: Three orbs for one card makes a pretty solid value package. Always generates a useful orb no matter the situation even if you don't always want all three of them. This creates a versatile card that has utility in every situation even though it's not the best card for any use case.

RAINBOW_RING.Commentary: A well-balanced deck can use this to gain stats over time and dominate in longer combats.  Particularly effective if you can generate new Power cards during combat.

RALLY.Commentary: An extremely efficient block option even if you only have 2 players.  A must-take in 3- or 4-player games.

RAMPAGE.Commentary: A single-card damage plan that can work quite well with Aggression or with a lot of Exhaust to redraw it frequently.

RATTLE.Commentary: Initially underwhelming but can scale to very significant damage in the right deck.  Great with Poke to give it Retain or Dredge to fetch this alongside other Osty attacks.

RAZOR_TOOTH.Commentary: Extremely strong Relic for any deck that re-draws its cards quickly.  Cards with Replay will immediately get the effect of the Upgrade.

REANIMATE.Commentary: Huge summon for one card.  Great in any build trying to stack Osty HP.

REAP.Commentary: Tons of damage for one card draw, and the Retain effect means you can keep this in hand until it finishes the fight or until you have spare energy to use on it.

REAPER_FORM.Commentary: Think of this as double attack damage.  Despite the upside, the cost makes this tricky to play.

REAVE.Commentary: An adequate pairing of Soul generation and damage, but Necrobinder has better ways of doing either.  Good enough on Floor 1.

REBOOT.Commentary: Reshuffling all your cards is sometimes a downside since you may get a worse draw order than before.  Upgrading for +2 cards drawn makes this a lot better.

REBOUND.Commentary: Passable damage, plus a useful effect that you can use to re-play your most impactful card.  The card placed on top can either be played next turn or drawn into and played immediately.  You can also play this last to avoid putting any card on top.

RED_MASK.Commentary: Useful for lowering enemy damage on Turn 1 or for removing enemy Artifact.

RED_SKULL.Commentary: Extremely powerful effect when active.  If you have this, it may be worth intentionally taking damage to ensure you start the next combat at 50% HP.

REFINE_BLADE.Commentary: A solid Forge amount combined with next-turn energy to let you play the sword.  Quite useful for building up a big blade in longer fights.

REFLECT.Commentary: A huge block number paired with a useful secondary effect makes this a very good card in almost any deck that can afford the Star cost.  One of Regent's best defensive tools.

REFLEX.Commentary: Turn your discard into positive draw!  You probably want three or more discard sources before clicking this. Gives block with Intimidating Helmet.

REFRACT.Commentary: Tons of damage output in a single card.  You get big damage to one target and area damage to everyone else.  The cost is prohibitive but it's worth picking up in Act I anyway.  Much better once you have other energy-generating cards.

REGALITE.Commentary: Great block output when paired with Regent's numerous card creation sources.

REGAL_PILLOW.Commentary: Very good healing that you only get when you would heal anyway.  In runs that are struggling, this can be a lifesaver.

REND.Commentary: This card really pops off if you can get three or more debuffs on the enemy.  A variety of potions can be used situationally to get an extra debuff or two.

REPTILE_TRINKET.Commentary: Strength for one turn is a decent enough bonus, but the Potion requirement really puts a damper on how useful this can be.  Can be clutch for bursting down a Boss or Elite with Potion Belt.

RESONANCE.Commentary: Both effects of this card are useful, but this card still doesn't feel that impactful when you play it compared to other cards with a similar Star cost.  Great in multiplayer.

RESTLESSNESS.Commentary: The upside of this card is quite strong, but for most characters it's quite hard to play every card in your hand.  More reliable if you can Exhaust or Discard cards from your hand.  Can be used to make an infinite combo.

RICOCHET.Commentary: Fairly underwhelming compared to other Sly options.  Much more viable if you enhance the damage per hit with Strength or an enchantment.

RIGHT_HAND_HAND.Commentary: This gets decent value if your deck has numerous expensive cards, but is underwhelming on its own.  Nice combo with Rattle.

RINGING_TRIANGLE.Commentary: Allows you to Retain excess Block or Power cards that you may have drawn turn 1 but not played.  Gets better if you draw additional cards on turn 1.

RIPPLE_BASIN.Commentary: An excellent source of added Block for decks that don't rely heavily on Attacks.  Very useful in helping you play Power cards.

RIP_AND_TEAR.Commentary: Very efficient damage for the energy cost.  Best with Vulnerable or Strength to further increase the damage,

ROCKET_PUNCH.Commentary: Extremely powerful once you have any source of status generation.  Since you don't need to draw this at the same time as the status card, you can use a single status generator to support multiple Rocket Punch.  All for One and Feral will return this card to your hand if it is discounted.

ROLLING_BOULDER.Commentary: Slow and steady damage that is a nice answer to many boss fights.  Won't do much in shorter fights, so don't rely on it for AoE damage.

ROYALTIES.Commentary: 30 gold per fight adds up quick and can be spent on card removes to counter the downside of having this in your deck.  Think of this as 1-2 relics per act.

ROYAL_GAMBLE.Commentary: Spicy star generation that requires other stars to get online.  Excellent as part of a larger engine in a star-heavy deck.  Best to upgrade in decks that don't have tons of draw.

ROYAL_STAMP.Commentary: An expensive price to pay for Enchanting one card but potentially worth it for the right target.  Good choices are powerful Block cards that you want to Retain or powerful Debuff cards that you want to play turn 1.

RUINED_HELMET.Commentary: Doubles the first Strength gain from any source, including Potions or other Relics.  Make sure to use your biggest boost first!

RUNIC_CAPACITOR.Commentary: Doubling your base orb slots allows you to get much more value from focus or from cards that scale with your number of orbs.  A must-have for any deck with many Channel effects.

RUNIC_PYRAMID.Commentary: Retaining your Hand lets you better utilize Block cards, combo cards and conditional cards alike!  Avoid the problem of a full Hand by adding 0-cost cards or Energy-generating cards.

RUPTURE.Commentary: An extremely fast source of Strength gain in the right build.  Works extremely well with Tear Asunder as a win condition.  Best with small self-pings like Breakthrough or Crimson Mantle.

SACRIFICE.Commentary: This requires you to have invested in Osty to produce real block, but also wipes out any investment you've achieved.  Seems only useful as a last-ditch block effort.

SAI.Commentary: Consistent block output can help any deck perform better.  Always worth at least considering as an option.

SALVO.Commentary: Retaining your hand is useful, but this card just isn't worth paying gold for.  Pretty good if you get it from Neow.

SAND_CASTLE.Commentary: Random upgrades are likely to hit Starter cards and be effectively wasted.  Much better if some Starter cards are already removed or Upgraded.

SCARE.Commentary: A low-impact card that is nice if you have a surplus of card draw.  Useful with Tracking to activate bonus damage on multiple enemies.

SCAVENGE.Commentary: Defect's only method to Exhaust cards mid-combat.  Can be used to set up infinite combos or to get rid of pesky Curse cards.  Works best with good card draw effects.

SCOURGE.Commentary: Doom seems quite efficient compared to dealing damage directly - 13 effective damage for 1 energy is very high, but you must account for the delayed effect and block for an additional turn to use it properly.

SCRAPE.Commentary: If you have multiple 0-cost cards in your deck this can be a great way to find them quickly.  Not great without several potential targets.  You can also use this with Hologram to fetch discarded cards that you want to play.

SCRAWL.Commentary: The definitive BEST card draw card.  Well worth paying 200 gold for in many situations.

SCREAMING_FLAGON.Commentary: Offers a lot of damage but is surprisingly hard to activate.  Most decks cannot empty their hand on most turns, and Curse or Status cards further complicate use of this Relic.  Good if you can Discard or Exhaust cards from your Hand.

SCROLL_BOXES.Commentary: Unreliable since you must take all three cards together.  You will usually end up with one card that is dead weight in the deck.

SCULPTING_STRIKE.Commentary: The secondary effect is quite flexible - use it on your main cards to activate Ethereal synergies, or use it on starter or curse cards to let them Exhaust at end of turn.

SEAL_OF_GOLD.Commentary: If you run out of Gold then you won't get Energy anymore.  You'll need to carefully manage a stockpile to avoid running out.  Don't even think about buying things at the Shop.

SEANCE.Commentary: Allows you to thin the deck each time you draw this.  Also nice for stacking Ethereal card plays for Banshee's Cry or Spirit of Ash.

SEA_GLASS.Commentary: A fun way to create silly combos across 2 colors.  Seeing 5 rare cards at once can be a very strong boost to your deck as well.

SECOND_WIND.Commentary: Not amazing unless you gain a benefit from Exhaust effects.  This is useful for dealing with enemies that add Status cards to your deck.  Lots of damage with Juggernaut.

SECRET_TECHNIQUE.Commentary: Find a block card on a crucial turn or get some debuffs set up for later in the fight.  Especially helpful if you have any per-card effects in play.

SECRET_WEAPON.Commentary: Fetching a specific attack is useful but not really worth buying at full price for most decks.  The upgraded version is nice if you can return it from your discard pile.

SEEKER_STRIKE.Commentary: The selective draw effect of this can be useful to help you get whatever you need at the current moment.  Not really worth it unless you need another attack.

SEEKING_EDGE.Commentary: A bit of an awkward card but can be clutch in specific fights.  If you're running a sword deck and have no area damage yet, this might just be what you need.

SELF_FORMING_CLAY.Commentary: Very useful whether you're dealing damage to yourself with cards or simply taking chip damage from enemies.  Best with per-turn powers like Inferno or Crimson Mantle.

SENTRY_MODE.Commentary: Creating a 0-cost Ethereal Osty attack allows you to activate synergies relating to either Osty or Ethereal.

SERE_TALON.Commentary: Wishes can get key Powers in play early, but the random Curse cards will slow you down.  Still potentially worth it if you have one or two really good cards to fetch.

SERPENT_FORM.Commentary: Expensive and unwieldly to play, but a very solid source of damage if you can get it down.  Great hit from a Power Potion.

SETUP_STRIKE.Commentary: A passable early-game attack that can combo well if you have a lot of other attacks to play.  Works well with Anger or Spite.

SEVEN_STARS.Commentary: Regent has a number of ways to make cards free, and this card is bonkers if you don't have to pay for it.  Casting this the hard way is potentially still worth it, but you have to prepare adequately.

SEVERANCE.Commentary: Decent damage combined with very effective soul generation.  Takeable in the early game and useful throughout.

SHADOWMELD.Commentary: Incredible defensive value for a single card.  Play this first followed by the block you want to double.

SHADOW_SHIELD.Commentary: Combines block and Dark into an extremely efficient package.  This card can singlehandedly carry Act I.

SHADOW_STEP.Commentary: Very useful multiplier for attacks. Obscene damage output if combined with Tracking.  Badly wants an upgrade.

SHARED_FATE.Commentary: Great at lowering enemy damage output, and most Necrobinder builds won't mind losing some Strength to pay for it.  Excellent in Multiplayer.

SHATTER.Commentary: Very effective area damage and burst orb output for 1 energy.  Really shines with Glass orbs.

SHINING_STRIKE.Commentary: A better version of Solar Strike?  Putting this card on top is not always desirable, so be careful when you play this.

SHOCKWAVE.Commentary: An extremely efficient and effective source of debuffs for almost any fight.  Well worth the upgrade for boss combats.

SHOVEL.Commentary: Fun in concept but suffers greatly from opportunity cost.  Upgrading your best card is more reliable in most situations.  Awesome with the Miniature Tent.

SHROUD.Commentary: Not a ton of block unless you've got numerous Doom sources.  Particularly good with Oblivion or Reaper Form.

SHRUG_IT_OFF.Commentary: Block plus draw, what's not to love?  One of the most reliable block options for Clad.

SHURIKEN.Commentary: Gives you escalating damage if you can spam a lot of Attack cards.  Best with bonus Energy or 0-cost cards.

SIC_EM.Commentary: The summon effect is useful in theory but is very difficult to make use of in practice.  Needs a lot of other Osty attacks to work.

SIGNAL_BOOST.Commentary: Note that you don't have to play the doubled power on the same turn as this card.  Particularly good for doubling Echo Form.

SIGNET_RING.Commentary: Reliably nets you Relics, Cards or Potions of your choice to tackle the end of the game.  Always great if you can get to one Shop early, better with two or more Shops.

SILKEN_TRESS.Commentary: You get to start your run with a super-powerful card.  Powers and 2+ cost cards are best, but even a lousy Common card is very strong if played twice.  Trivializes a lot of Act I.

SILVER_CRUCIBLE.Commentary: Big benefit at a big cost.  This is effectively -1 Relic for your run, so it's mostly worth it when the Upgraded cards let you fight an extra Elite in Act I.  Great for maps without a Rest Site early.

SKEWER.Commentary: A 'dense' attack card that can serve as an energy sink.  Multiply the output with Vulnerable, Tracking, or Shadow Step.

SKIM.Commentary: Definitive no-nonsense draw that works extremely well with Defect's numerous energy-generating cards.  Not a great pick in Act I.

SLEIGHT_OF_FLESH.Commentary: Incredible damage output when combined with Necro's wide array of debuff effects.  Note that Doom is a debuff.

SLICE.Commentary: Damage, for free!  Nothing special about this, is mostly outclassed by other attack options but will work in a pinch.

SLING_OF_COURAGE.Commentary: A solid damage boost against Elite combats for Attack-focused decks.  Can be used to help you hunt for more Relics or to patch a weak spot against a particular foe.

SMALL_CAPSULE.Commentary: Not every Relic will help you right away but this is still one of the surest ways to get started.

SMOKESTACK.Commentary: Very solid area damage for a status-generating build.  Especially nice with Overlock, Turbo, or Boost Away.

SNAKEBITE.Commentary: Retain is a nice effect to have on a 2-cost damage card so that you can find a window to play it.  Much better with an upgrade.  Almost always useful against the Act I boss.

SNAP.Commentary: The attack is underwhelming but adding Retain to a key block card or combo card can be crucial for some fights.  The affected card keeps Retain for the whole battle.

SNEAKY.Commentary: Passive block output that is excellent with 3 or 4 players.

SNECKO_EYE.Commentary: The Confusion aspect of this Relic is a downside - the 2 draw per turn is the upside.  You get more random card costs but less random draws.  Any deck with a couple of 2-cost cards should consider this.

SNECKO_SKULL.Commentary: A nice bonus to output for any deck with more than one Poison card.  Particularly excellent with Noxious Fumes, Corrosive Wave or Bouncing Flask.

SOLAR_STRIKE.Commentary: A decent star generator when upgraded.  Works with Strike Dummy and does decent enough damage early on.

SOUL_STORM.Commentary: Surprisingly slow to get going for a rare attack.  Worth it only if you're generating at least five souls per deck cycle.

SOW.Commentary: Passable early-game area damage to get through your first Elite or hard pool fights.

SOZU.Commentary: Can be very good if you already have a couple of good Potions.  The more empty Potion slots you currently have, the worse this is.

SPARKLING_ROUGE.Commentary: A great stat boost if a bit slow to come online.  The Dexterity is more useful for most decks than the Strength, but some will appreciate both parts.

SPECTRUM_SHIFT.Commentary: Kind of like 1 draw per turn, but colorless cards are somewhat higher value than normal cards.  Much better if you have synergies for colorless cards or card generation such as Pillar of Creation.  Notably, this can generate more power cards for you to scale with.

SPEEDSTER.Commentary: The damage adds up fast if you have draw sources.  Acrobatics is the best enabler, but look for Calculated Gamble, Backflip and Prepared as well.

SPIKED_GAUNTLETS.Commentary: A useful way to catch up for decks that don't have many Powers.  If you have more than three Power cards then this may not be worth it.

SPINNER.Commentary: Consistent area damage and orb Channeling provides consistent value across any combat.  Upgrade to get immediate value.

SPIRIT_OF_ASH.Commentary: Excellent source of block for any deck with at least a couple Ethereal cards.  Combine with Sculpting Strike to activate on any card of your choosing.

SPITE.Commentary: A 0-cost attack you can take to throw down more damage in the early game.  Becomes a lot better if you can activate the secondary effect with Crimson Mantle or Inferno.

SPLASH.Commentary: A shockingly effective damage source that is quite flexible from combat to combat.  Frequently creates 2- or 3-cost attacks for free.

SPOILS_OF_BATTLE.Commentary: Draw 2 is quite valuable for Regent if you have any kind of energy surplus.  The Forge amount isn't high so try not to think of this as primarily a damage card.

SPUR.Commentary: Very good Osty HP for one mana with the added benefit of Retain.  To get the most of this Osty must lose HP without dying, so other Summon effects are needed alongside this.

SQUEEZE.Commentary: Becomes massive with enough Osty attacks in the deck.  Especially nice with Clone, but you can also scale this every turn with Sentry Mode.

STACK.Commentary: In early game this card doesn't block for significantly more than other blocks.  If you are generating a lot of status cards or if your deck has a large total number of cards it can end up blocking for a ton!

STAMPEDE.Commentary: Useful for playing huge attacks like Bludgeon or Mangle without having to pay their cost.  Best if you can Exhaust other attacks in hand to guarantee a specific target.

STARDUST.Commentary: The ultimate payoff to a deck that can generate a lot of stars.  Works really well with Royal Gamble.  Scale the damage with Strength or Vigor for maximum effect.

STOKE.Commentary: Outstanding for activating exhaust effects like Feel No Pain or Dark Embrace.  Creating random cards can make new powers for you or otherwise bail you out by making an immediately useful card.

STOMP.Commentary: A very nice pickup to help with multi-enemy fights.  You can pay full price if you really need to, but goes best with some 0-cost attacks to make it cheaper.

STONE_ARMOR.Commentary: A steady source of block for the early game, but less effective as the run goes on. Fun to duplicate.

STONE_CALENDAR.Commentary: Though the damage is big, it arrives too slowly to be relevant in most combats.  Mostly helpful against Boss enemies.

STONE_CRACKER.Commentary: Two Upgraded cards per fight ends up being a significant boost to your performance.  Better with fewer total cards in your deck.

STONE_HUMIDIFIER.Commentary: Significantly better if you can path to more Rest Sites in Act I.  This lets you path more aggressively and take more risks thanks to the added healing you'll get.

STORM.Commentary: Overwhelm your opponents with tons of powers!  Can be a continual source of damage with Creative AI.  You probably want at least three other powers before picking this.

STORM_OF_STEEL.Commentary: Decent damage per card on its own but really shines if you can discard Sly cards.  Tingsha or Tough Bandages make this much better as well.

STORYBOOK.Commentary: Don't worry about the Max HP loss - even if you play Brightest Flame every time you draw it, you'll have plenty left at the end.  Upgrade the added card ASAP for maximum output.

STRANGLE.Commentary: A solid enough attack that fits well into Shiv or Sly decks that play many cards.

STRATAGEM.Commentary: Smaller decks will trigger the effect more often, but large decks benefit more from choosing any card.  Either way, this is 1 draw per deck reshuffle.  Also useful for being a 0-cost power when upgraded.

STRAWBERRY.Commentary: It's tasty!  Nice enough if you need some HP right now, or if your Max HP was reduced earlier.

STRIKE_DEFECT.Commentary: Defect's worst card.  Get rid of these as soon as you can.

STRIKE_DUMMY.Commentary: Adds a very significant amount of damage to your starting cards, making this an excellent Act I relic.  This can help keep your Strikes relevant in the late game if combined with other improvements.

STRIKE_IRONCLAD.Commentary: Ironclad's Strikes are useful all game.  They have synergies with other cards and can be Enchanted to be more useful.

STRIKE_NECROBINDER.Commentary: Necrobinder has a defense-heavy playstyle and these will only get in your way.  Remove these ASAP and lean on Unleash or better attacks.

STRIKE_REGENT.Commentary: Necessary for the first few floors but mostly gets in your way.  One of your best remove targets.

STRIKE_SILENT.Commentary: Silent hates having 5 of these to start.  While you need them for early encounters, you'll want to quickly remove a couple and replace them with better damage.

STURDY_CLAMP.Commentary: Allows your Block to be much more efficient by ensuring no block points are wasted and letting you Block when the enemy is attacking. Good for almost any deck.

SUBROUTINE.Commentary: A steady flow of energy for decks with many powers.  Multiple copies can allow you to gain energy for each power you play.  Combo with Creative AI.

SUCKER_PUNCH.Commentary: Damage plus weaken is a reasonable combo, but this card does not excel at either purpose.

SUMMON_FORTH.Commentary: One of the few ways to play Sovereign Blade multiple times in one turn.  Kind of like Forge + draw 1.

SUNDER.Commentary: A broadly useful tool for picking off low-HP enemies or minions.  Also works well with Beam Cell or Echo Form to provide damage against a boss.

SUPERCRITICAL.Commentary: Huge burst energy that works especially well with good card draw or with Hologram to combo this with expensive cards.

SUPERMASSIVE.Commentary: This attack underperforms unless you have significant card generation.  Works well with Crash Landing and Spectrum Shift.

SUPPRESS.Commentary: Big upfront damage plus Weak that practically lasts all fight.  What's not to love?

SURVIVOR.Commentary: A starter card that is relevant all game long.  With an upgrade this is one of Silent's best starter cards.  The discard is also useful for activating Sly effects.

SWEEPING_BEAM.Commentary: Functional if underwhelming area damage.  Won't actually solve multi-enemy fights unless you upgrade it and/or play it multiple times.

SWORD_BOOMERANG.Commentary: Benefits a ton from Strength or Enchantments.  The low initial damage and random targeting make this a liability in the early game.

SWORD_SAGE.Commentary: Double your Sovereign Blade output!  Absolutely massive in a Forge-centric deck.  Also causes Parry to block twice.

SYMBIOTIC_VIRUS.Commentary: Starting with a bonus orb increases the value of cards that depending on having multiple orb types such as Compile Driver.  The orb itself can deal decent damage too.

SYNCHRONIZE.Commentary: The biggest source of temporary focus.  Extremely strong way to improve Frost and Glass orbs, but you need to have at least 2 orb types to get proper value.

SYNTHESIS.Commentary: Mediocre damage stapled to a highly conditional energy bonus.  Most useful to sneak Echo Form or Creative AI into play.

TACTICIAN.Commentary: Free energy on discard is very powerful in any deck with a lot of draw/discard.  Acrobatics and Tools of the Trade are the best enablers.

TAG_TEAM.Commentary: If your allies have expensive attacks, this can be extremely powerful.  You will need to coordinate to properly make the most of the effect.

TANK.Commentary: Actually increases the total damage dealt by enemies if you use this in a 2-player game.  Only really worth it with 4 players, and you need VERY good block to survive after playing this.

TANXS_WHISTLE.Commentary: A very expensive one-time stun.  Not really worth it unless you're able to get more than one copy of the card somehow.

TAUNT.Commentary: Seems difficult to use both effects of the card at the same time.  I like this for extending Vulnerable on enemies during defensive turns, rather than as a way to apply Vulnerable initially.  Great with Body Slam.

TEAR_ASUNDER.Commentary: A very nice payoff for a build that is dealing small amounts of self-damage frequently.  Works especially well with Strength.

TEMPEST.Commentary: Massive damage payoff when combined with Defect's numerous energy-generating cards.  Nice way to jump-start Voltaic.

TERRAFORMING.Commentary: Provides a massive damage boost to multihit cards.  Use with Radiate, Stardust, Heavenly Drill, or even certain event cards.  Note that the effect carries across turns, so you can wait until your best card arrives or even stack it multiple times.

TESLA_COIL.Commentary: Great bonus damage in a deck running lots of Lightning.  Works especially well with temporary Focus boosts.

THE_ABACUS.Commentary: Can be used to generate massive amounts of Block for decks that cycle very quickly.  Any deck with 20 or fewer cards will appreciate the added Block.

THE_BOMB.Commentary: Big damage, but you have to be able to wait.  Don't rely on this for AoE damage.  Best against bosses.

THE_COURIER.Commentary: Each type of card in the Merchant (Attack, Skill, Power) is replaced by another card of the same type.  Buying many Powers in particular can be quite useful.  If you get a huge amount of Gold somehow, you can break the game by buying all the relics.

THE_GAMBIT.Commentary: The key to using this card is understanding that you can play it more than once.  If you can reliably play this every single turn you'll never need any other block.  Easier said than done.

THE_HUNT.Commentary: Extra card rewards are excellent, but it may be tricky to land the killing blow with this especially if you have Poison.  Well-Laid Plans can help a lot.  Guaranteed rare card from bosses.

THE_SCYTHE.Commentary: Becomes ridiculous damage eventually if you grab it in Act I.  It can be worth seeking out more combats to scale it higher.

THE_SEALED_THRONE.Commentary: Stars galore!  A great pick for your boss reward as long as you can spend the stars you're making.  Arguably one of Regent's best cards.

THE_SMITH.Commentary: Although this is very expensive, the added sword damage is massive.  Well worth it if you have Stars to spend and any Forge support cards.

THINKING_AHEAD.Commentary: Think of this like being able to Retain 1 card.  While the manipulation effect can be handy, this card doesn't do enough compared to other colorless cards to be worth buying.

THRASH.Commentary: The damage added to this card includes your Strength, Relics, and Enchantments.  The damage of this card can scale very rapidly while also thinning the deck so that you can re-draw it later.

THROWING_AXE.Commentary: Nice for getting a second copy of a key Power in play on turn 1.  Best with cards that are Innate so that you know what you'll be doubling.

THRUMMING_HATCHET.Commentary: A reasonably-efficient attack that makes itself continually available as long as you keep playing it.  Especially useful if discounted or if your deck is thin on attack cards.

THUNDER.Commentary: Solid bonus damage in any deck that creates a lot of Lightning.  You can also multiply the effect with Quadcast or Multicast on a Lightning.

THUNDERCLAP.Commentary: Underwhelming damage, but the primary advantage is being able to utilize powers that interact with Vulnerable.  Draws cards like crazy with Vicious.

TIMES_UP.Commentary: Compare to an effect that doubles the enemy Doom.  Effectively kills enemies that have doom equal to half their HP.  Upgrading for Retain is worth it.

TINGSHA.Commentary: Potentially massive damage in decks that are draw/discard focused.  Particularly amazing with Calculated Gamble.

TINY_MAILBOX.Commentary: A great way to get back in shape when you're low health and out of Potions.  Particularly good with extra Potion slots so that you can stock up.

TOASTY_MITTENS.Commentary: Very unreliable because of the random Exhaust.  You will want to win fights quickly with the Strength and have a backup plan in case your key cards are Exhausted.

TOOLBOX.Commentary: More options on turn 1 is always useful.  You get to see the enemy actions on turn 1 before you make a choice.  This can generate Power cards for you to play.

TOOLS_OF_THE_TRADE.Commentary: Discard every turn goes crazy with Sly synergies.  Upgrading to 0-cost makes this pickable for a wide variety of decks.

TOUCH_OF_OROBAS.Commentary: Most characters benefit quite a bit from the relic upgrade.  Necrobinder likes this the most.

TOUGH_BANDAGES.Commentary: Allows you to pick up every draw/discard card that you see.  With the right deck this can provide all the Block that you need.

TOXIC_EGG.Commentary: Skill is the most common type of card, so this egg can provide tons of upgrades!  Consider Upgraded Colorless cards when you see them in the shop if you have this.

TOY_BOX.Commentary: A nice initial boost that will fade away completely by the end of the run.  Useful for getting up to speed in Act II but you'll need to fight Elites to stay relevant later.

TRACKING.Commentary: Excellent damage output for any deck with consistent Weak.  Multiplies bonus damage from any other source, such as Strength, enchantments, or relics.

TRANSFIGURE.Commentary: Especially good with Danse Macabre or Intimidating Helmet as this both increases card cost and activates multiple times.  Broadly useful for doubling scaling cards such as powers or cards that benefit from repeat plays like No Escape.

TRASH_TO_TREASURE.Commentary: The random nature of the channeled orb might be daunting, but spamming a bunch of orbs for free is always good value.  A must-have for a deck with many status generators.

TREMBLE.Commentary: Easy way to get Vulnerable for cheap, very nice if you have big expensive attacks.  Cheap way to get a card in the Exhaust pile for related synergies.

TRI_BOOMERANG.Commentary: Excellent for decks whose damage strategy revolves around a few specific Attacks.  Won't do much if your damage comes from Power or Skill cards.

TRUE_GRIT.Commentary: Solid block for the early game that synergizes well with block effects and Exhaust triggers.  Add a Feel No Pain or Dark Embrace later to make the most of this.

TUNGSTEN_ROD.Commentary: Comparatively minor health savings compared to other Relics that heal or generate Block.  If you become Intangible while having this relic, you become immune to all damage.

TUNING_FORK.Commentary: Excellent source of added Block for any deck.  The counter persists across fights so you can set it up to activate on the first Skill of a combat.

TURBO.Commentary: No-nonsense energy right now with a penalty that only applies later.  Can be part of a status deck, or you can simply use Hologram to get the Void to exhaust without losing energy.

TWIN_STRIKE.Commentary: Decent enough early game damage that benefits twice from Strength.  Very nice with Strike Dummy.

TWISTED_FUNNEL.Commentary: A useful headstart on dealing damage for poison decks especially.  Also useful for removing Artifact at combat start.

TYRANNY.Commentary: Card draw and deck thinning all in one.  This even lets you get rid of particularly troublesome curses like Bad Luck or Enthralled.  Great against status-adding enemies.

ULTIMATE_DEFEND.Commentary: An overall very efficient source of block.   Even better with an upgrade.

ULTIMATE_STRIKE.Commentary: Good enough damage to carry many Act I encounters on its own.  Significantly improves with an upgrade.

UNCEASING_TOP.Commentary: Gives you escalating damage if you can spam a lot of Attack cards.  Best with bonus Energy or 0-cost cards.

UNDEATH.Commentary: Very useful self-duplicating block. This is an especially good card for Enchantments that have a one-time effect as the copy is created before the Enchantment is consumed on the original.

UNDYING_SIGIL.Commentary: Significantly reduces the damage you take on the final turn if you're a Doom build.  Not worth it if you're not running Doom or if you can already block on the last turn without trouble.

UNLEASH.Commentary: This is your best way to turn Summon into damage.  This card is useful all game and can even be your main damage engine for boss combats.

UNMOVABLE.Commentary: Good in almost any deck.  If your block cards are sparse, you'll appreciate doubling whatever you draw.  If you have lots of block, you can use this on your most impactful ones for maximum effect.

UNRELENTING.Commentary: Decent damage plus an effect that works well with Clad's big attacks like Bludgeon or Mangle.  You can save the effect across multiple turns.

UNSETTLING_LAMP.Commentary: Doubles the effect of the entire card, so cards that apply multiple Debuffs will have all of those Debuffs doubled.  Extremely good if used on a damaging debuff like Poison or Doom.  You may need to avoid playing cards with minor Debuffs to make the most of this.

UNTOUCHABLE.Commentary: Excellent block output if you can play it for free with Sly.  In a pinch, you can pay for it to save some HP as well.

UPPERCUT.Commentary: Ironclad's only source of Weak, which makes this a must for bosses.  Nice for breaking through Artifact on enemies.

UPROAR.Commentary: Offers efficient damage in theory but is too unreliable in practice.  The target of the played attack is also random.  To make the most of this, remove all your Strikes and don't add low-cost attacks.

UP_MY_SLEEVE.Commentary: Useful damage output in decks that re-draw their cards frequently, but paying the initial 2 cost can be a challenge.

VAJRA.Commentary: Solid added damage for decks relying on Attacks, especially ones dealing relatively low damage per hit.

VAMBRACE.Commentary: Make your first Block card count!  Applies to all instances of Block from the first card, doubling the full effect of cards like Dodge and Roll.  This will multiply the value of any added Dexterity.

VEILPIERCER.Commentary: Useful for playing Demesne, but most other times this is an attack that banks 1 energy for later.

VELVET_CHOKER.Commentary: Most decks can't play 6 cards per turn easily, so the downside can be ignored.  Very bad if you are drawing or generating lots of cards per turn (like Shivs).

VENERABLE_TEA_SET.Commentary: Solid Turn 1 energy that only applies sometimes.  Very useful in Boss combats, or Elite combats that line up after a Rest Site.

VENERATE.Commentary: While this isn't the best way to make Stars, some is still better than none!  Consider upgrading this early if you pick up some Star spenders.

VERY_HOT_COCOA.Commentary: Very good if you can spend the Energy on expensive cards or with lots of card draw.  Most decks will not be able to use all of it.

VEXING_PUZZLEBOX.Commentary: Can generate any card from your character, including 3-cost Powers.  Usually useful and will randomly trivialize combats by making the perfect card for the situation.

VICIOUS.Commentary: A massive source of draw that can be used to enable energy-generating cards in your build.  You only need 2 or 3 sources of Vulnerable to make this excellent.  A must-upgrade.

VITRUVIAN_MINION.Commentary: Incredibly strong as it doubles the value of the entire card after additions such as Strength, Vigor, or Dexterity.  Super worthwhile if you have even two sources of Minion cards.

VOID_FORM.Commentary: Allows you to ignore star costs as well as energy costs.  Fill your deck with super-expensive cards and just throw them down every turn!

VOLLEY.Commentary: A reasonably effective attack that serves as a solid way to spend extra energy.  Much more powerful with an upgrade or Enchantment.

VOLTAIC.Commentary: A one-card solution to longer combats.  Duplicate with Echo Form for triple damage!

WAR_HAMMER.Commentary: Offers no advantage until after you've beaten an Elite, which may be too late to prevent you from losing a ton of HP.  Can be very strong if you kill 3+ Elites.

WAR_PAINT.Commentary: Often upgrades 2 Defends, but the added defense is still consistently useful.  Even better if other skills are upgraded instead.

WELL_LAID_PLANS.Commentary: Retaining cards has multiple benefits.  You can line up cards with enemy actions to optimize their effect, set up combos between multiple cards, or simply benefit from having more total cards in hand.

WHETSTONE.Commentary: Likely to upgrade 2 Strikes.  Can be quite good if you manage to upgrade other Attacks, but this is rarely reliable.

WHIRLWIND.Commentary: A great card for dealing with multi-enemy combats, as well as a way to turn damage into energy efficiently alongside cards like Expect a Fight.   Needs an upgrade.

WHISPERING_EARRING.Commentary: Vakuu will play your cards from left to right on turn 1.  This often results in taking damage because he didn't block or missing out on playing key Power cards.  Innate cards work very well since Vakuu will always play those first.

WHITE_BEAST_STATUE.Commentary: A steady trickle of Potions helps you stay stocked up while also using them in combat regularly.  Having this makes visiting combat rooms more rewarding.

WHITE_NOISE.Commentary: Always has a chance to bail you out by generating a great power.  Especially good if you're spamming powers with Subroutine or Storm.

WHITE_STAR.Commentary: Makes Elites far more rewarding but doesn't give you any benefits until you actually beat one.  Make sure you can actually win before you go hunting for Rares.

WINGED_BOOTS.Commentary: This one very much depends on the map you've been given for Act I.  Consider taking it if you can get an extra Elite or Rest Site.

WING_CHARM.Commentary: Ends up adding a ton of card draw to your deck by the end of the game.  Many otherwise-questionable cards become extremely useful with draw 1 attached, especially cards that Exhaust or Power cards.  Allows you to pick cards more aggressively.

WISP.Commentary: Trading one draw for one energy is often worth it on Necrobinder to help play expensive cards. Also good alongside lots of Souls.

WRAITH_FORM.Commentary: Effectively three turns of invincibility that you can use to deploy more power cards or to deal damage.  Try to have a plan to win the fight once your Intangible wears off.

WROUGHT_IN_WAR.Commentary: Decent enough to take as an early-game common, but not an ideal card for many situations.

YUMMY_COOKIE.Commentary: Hard to argue against 4 Upgrades of your choosing.  Pick your 4 best cards, with Energy and draw Upgrades being especially valuable.

ZAP.Commentary: A very solid source of damage for Defect's early combats.  Worth an upgrade early on to get a free orb each time you draw it.
